# Ready72h

> Household preparedness planner for the first 72 hours of a crisis (power outage, flood, network blackout), based on official guidance from Sweden (MSB), Germany (BBK) and Poland (RCB). Printable PDF + offline app, PL/EN/DE/ES, pay what you want from 2 PLN.

## Free calculators
- [Emergency water calculator](https://ready72h.com/tools/water-calculator/)
- [Emergency cash calculator](https://ready72h.com/tools/emergency-cash-calculator/)

## Guides
- [How much cash should you keep at home for a blackout?](https://ready72h.com/guides/emergency-cash/): The Dutch central bank recommends €70 per adult and €30 per child to get through the first 72 hours. Sweden's Riksbank suggests, for example, 1,000 kronor in cash per adult.
- [What food to store for 72 hours without cooking?](https://ready72h.com/guides/food-for-72-hours-without-cooking/): Choose long-life food you can eat straight from the pack: canned meat, fish, vegetables and fruit, crackers, bars, nuts, dried fruit and peanut butter, plus a manual can opener and utensils. Ready.gov, BBK and Poland's RCB all point to food that needs no refrigeration, cooking or special preparation.
- [Emergency go-bag for wheelchair users, people with disabilities and older adults](https://ready72h.com/guides/go-bag-disability-older-adults/): If carrying a 10 kg backpack isn't realistic, plan around a lighter bag, the right repair and power kit for your equipment, and a support network of at least three nearby people who know how to help.
- [How to prepare for a power outage (blackout) at home](https://ready72h.com/guides/prepare-for-power-outage-blackout-at-home/): Prepare for a power outage with food that needs no cooking, water, charged power banks, flashlights, a battery or crank radio and some cash. Poland's government safety guide suggests home supplies for at least three days; BBK and Ready.gov add advice on warmth and safe habits.
- [How much water do you need for 72 hours?](https://ready72h.com/guides/water-72-hours/): Plan at least 2 litres of water per person per day for drinking and cooking – that's 6 litres per person for 72 hours. With basic hygiene, plan around 3 litres a day.
